newsitem.title: ITALY: Real-life Don Camillo won't toll bells for red.
newsitem.headline: Real-life Don Camillo won't toll bells for red.

text.p: An Italian communist has been denied a church funeral by his Roman Catholic parish priest in a real-life rendering of the Don Camillo story.

Cesare Quattrocchi, a life-long communist who died aged 85 last Saturday, had to be buried at a different church when Don Antonio Pasquiarello turned his family away from their parish church of St John the Apostle in the town of Velletri, the Rome newspaper Il Messaggero reported on Wednesday.

"They denied him the church, and even refused to toll the church bells for his death," the newspaper quoted a member of Quattrochhi's family as saying. It said the family planned to complain to the local bishop.
The priest denied his decision was linked to the dead man's politics. "Bells don't toll for people who never went to church," Pasquiarello said.
Italian author Giovanni Guareschi's Don Camillo books, written in the 1950s, told comic tales of the squabbles between a village priest and its communist mayor.
